subject: Data locality & PII/PHI retention options for HealthBridge
messages:
From: Dr. Emily Park <emily.park@healthbridge.org>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Question: retention & redaction options for PII/PHI (regulated workload)

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HealthBridge is evaluating Redwood for a draft patient messaging feature. Before we proceed to procurement we need detail on two things for our security/compliance team:

1) Data residency: can all patient-derived content (including intermediate prompt history and KV cache) be restricted to US-only regions for both storage and processing? We are a US-covered entity and cannot have PHI processed outside the US.

2) Retention/deletion: what retention windows do you support out-of-the-box for generated logs, prompts, and model context? We need a documented deletion workflow: immediate deletion API, bulk purge, and how long artifacts (backups, snapshots) may persist. Evidence of deletion for audits is essential.

3) Redaction options: we need options for redaction/tokenization before data reaches the model (client-side), and server-side redaction if we host Private or Dedicated. What redaction tooling do you provide, and can you share a short playbook?

I attached a one-page scope doc (HealthBridge_Data_Scope_Summary.pdf) to help. Can you put together a short Q&A we can pass to our InfoSec?

Best,
Emily
Dr. Emily Park
Director, Product Security
HealthBridge

Subject: Re: Question: retention & redaction options for PII/PHI (regulated workload)

Hi Emily — thanks for the scope doc, looks straightforward. Looping in Laura (Product) and Neha (Security) to provide the details you requested. High level: yes, US-only processing is supported for Private deployments and for our Hosted offering we can pin to US regions and apply strict routing. Deletion and redaction options differ slightly between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private; below is an initial summary, we will follow up with a technical playbook and SOC2 evidence.

Quick summary:
- Residency: Private (VPC) = customer-managed network and data plane in your cloud region; Hosted = US-only tenancy options with contractual residency guarantees for enterprise customers; Dedicated = capacity reserved in US regions.
- Retention & deletion: deletion APIs available (immediate delete for indexed artifacts, configurable retention windows for logs), bulk purge scripts for Dedicated/Private, and we can provide deletion receipts for audit events.
- Redaction: client-side redaction/tokenization recommended (we provide SDK helpers), plus server-side pre-ingest redaction plug-ins for Private deployments; we can also enable automated PII detection and redact before caching.

Laura / Neha — can you produce a 1-page Q&A and attach the redaction playbook (v0.9) and SOC2 excerpts? Emily, we'll aim to get that back in 48 hours.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein | Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Markus + Emily — forwarding the initial reply and attaching the draft playbook. See the playbook for implementation options; below are the practical pieces HealthBridge normally asks for.

Attached: redaction_playbook_v0.9.docx

Implementation options (concise):
- Option A (Private VPC): Customer deploys Redwood Private into their AWS account in us-east-1. All inference, KV cache, and logs remain in your VPC/subnets. We install server-side redaction hooks that operate on pre-ingest traffic. Retention is customer-controlled; Redwood will not retain copies beyond configured retention windows and we provide deletion receipts.

- Option B (Dedicated Reserved): We reserve GPU capacity in a US region under a contract. Logs and backups are stored in our US tenancy, we can apply strict routing and offer a 30/90/365-day configurable retention for metadata and token logs. Backup snapshots are encrypted and retained per SLA; we can schedule scrub windows as part of the contract.

- Option C (Hosted with US tenancy + short retention): For lower-friction pilots we can host in US-only tenancy, with automated redaction hooks and a 30-day default retention for prompt logs; we can shorten that to 7 days for specific routes and provide deletion receipts via API.

Key technical notes:
- Deletion API: /v1/data/delete supports object-level deletion with async audit receipt (job id). For Private, the same API can be configured to call customer-defined lifecycle policies.
- Evidence: audit logs include job ids, timestamps, and hashes of deleted objects; we can provide signed deletion receipts for audits.
- Redaction: we support regex and ML-based PII detectors; tokenization (client-side) is recommended for the highest assurance.

Next steps: Neha will add security-specific caveats and required contract language. Markus — can you coordinate with Mike Ross on any legal constraints? Emily — any priority retention windows you want us to focus on (7/30/90/365 days)?

Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: retention & redaction options for PII/PHI (regulated workload)

Adding the security view for HealthBridge (draft for Emily):

- Residency guarantee: for Hosted/DED we include contractual language limiting processing and storage to US regions (listed explicitly). For Private, customer controls region.
- Retention defaults: Hosted default token logs = 30 days; Dedicated = configurable (30/90/365); Private = customer-controlled. We can implement shorter per-route overrides (7-day) and immediate-expiry (TTL=0) for sensitive routes.
- Deletion/integrity evidence: when deletion jobs complete we emit an audit event containing: job_id, timestamp, object_keys, SHA256(object) before deletion, operator_id. We store these audit events for 1 year by default (retention negotiable).
- Redaction capabilities:
  * Pre-ingest client-side tokenization SDK (recommended): replaces PHI with reversible tokens you control; we never see raw PHI.
  * Server-side ML PII detector + redaction plug-in: configurable sensitivity; can redact or mask before KV-cache or argmax sampling.

Caveats:
- Model caching: certain inference micro-optimizations rely on KV caches; if you enable server-side redaction we will prevent PHI from being stored in caches. If you require absolutely no in-memory PHI, Private is the recommended path and we will disable KV persistence.
- Backups & snapshots: Dedicated backups may exist for DR; we can scope backup retention or provide an encryption key that HealthBridge controls.

I'll attach a short security appendix and the SOC2 excerpt in a follow-up. Recommend Emily pick target retention windows (e.g., 7 days for prompts, 30 days for logs) and whether HealthBridge prefers tokenization or server-side redaction.

-Neha
Security, Redwood Inference
